primary event memory
if a DTC exists having a

agnosticMemoryDestinationPrimary

CodeProps.diagnosticMemory

[SWS_DM_00057] Availability of a user-defined event memory
Upstream requirements:
RS_Diag_04214, RS_Diag_04058
⌈
The DM shall support the
user-defined event memory
with the number
Diag-
nosticMemoryDestinationUserDefined.memoryId
if a DTC exists having a
DiagnosticMemoryDestinationUserDefined
with that user-defined number ref-
erenced by its
DiagnosticTroubleCodeProps.diagnosticMemory
.
⌋
The size of the different
event memories
is configurable by the DM configuration
parameters.
[SWS_DM_00920] Configuration of the event memory size
Upstream requirements:
RS_Diag_04064
⌈
The DM shall provide
event memories
of a size according to the configuration pa-
rameter
DiagnosticMemoryDestination.maxNumberOfEventEntries
, where
each single event memory entry is to be understood as the complete data set that
belongs to a DTC, including counters, cycles,
snapshot records
and
extended
data records
.
⌋

quence. Therefore the DM provides an overflow indication in case the

7.3.4.4.1
DTC
Introduction
A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) defines a unique identifier mapped to a
diagnostic
event
via
DiagnosticEventToTroubleCodeUdsMapping
. The DTC is used by
diagnostics, including e.g. UDS communication with an external tester, to uniquely
identify data within the
event memory
database.

DTC
s
Upstream requirements:
RS_Diag_04201
⌈
The existence of a
DiagnosticTroubleCodeUds
indicates that the DM shall sup-
port this DTC.
